title: Generic C1 Future Inextendibility Near Rotating Subextremal Kerr Spacetimes
main_claim: For each fixed Kerr center with M>0 and 0<a<M, there is eps_0>0 such that the p_10-ball U_{eps_0} of smooth, complete, two-ended vacuum data in a weighted smooth topology contains a dense G_delta set. Every datum in that set has a maximal globally hyperbolic development with no future C^1 extension (Theorem 2.3). The ambient extension may be nonvacuum.

issues.location: Sec. 4 Prop. bg:geometry (2) and Lemma bg:coefficients; used in Sec. 6 eq. energy:deformation-limits and energy:common-rate
issues.description: The common energy rate 2kappa+eta_0 in the bulk needs the low background quantities (ell_i+kappa, chi_i, b, and the differentiated connection terms) to tend to zero pointwise as min(t,v,-u)->infinity. The envelope estimate (bg:envelopes) only gives bounds by q+g_i(y_i) with summable g_i, and that alone does not give pointwise decay. The paper takes the pointwise limit as a separate conclusion (bg:low-limits) imported from the Foundation companion. The argument is valid given that citation, but this step depends on an external result rather than on anything proved in this paper.
issues.evidence: 'The following quantities are uniformly bounded, and tend to zero when t,|u|,|v|->infinity' (bg:low-limits), cited from Foundation in:low / in:pure-jets / in:higher

coverage: I read all of Secs. 1-9 in build/sections, and the appendix only by its role. These parts I checked in detail. (1) Baire/phase-space lemma, closedness of the tests A(O,B), the causal-homotopy diamond lemma, the small-developed-length transport bootstrap, and the exit-coverage proposition (C^1 exit -> uniform transport test on an open seed set). (2) The corner-ratio bounds: I re-derived e^{kappa y_i} p_i = (q0/kappa) A |Ydot_j|, the Cauchy-Schwarz bound on the integral of |Xi|, and the corner-seed null-set argument (section momenta pi_{Y1} = -q0 A Ydot_0/kappa^2, preservation of section symplectic forms by variable-time hitting maps, volume <= C_N r, Fatou). (3) Branch normalization: a_p ~ e^{-kappa T}, and the observer components (udot, p, Xi) are bounded in the boosted E-frame. (4) Energy section: the model identity dE/dt = int(-4c_n PV - 2kappa a|df|^2 + ...), giving a square-root rate of 2kappa over a time of about T/2; the common-rate construction; the Volterra propagator; the odd-forcing structure (the quadratic packet term cancels, leaving A^3 e^R and A^4 e^{2R}); and the exponent bookkeeping -3k/4, -13k/8, -3k/2, c = 3k/16 against A = e^{-7kT/8}. (5) Preparation: the signed constraint solve with one shared inverse K (odd correction cubic), the p_m unscaling cost, and the exterior late-support rate. (6) Attachment: whole-bridge Cauchy property and the absolute-shell root and backward Gronwall (eps_T/sqrt(a_p) -> 0). (7) Holonomy: the conversion formula for G, a full check of the seven negative-exponent triples and their vanishing/smallness, the developed length bound <= a_p h Q_T, the second holonomy coefficient = curvature (Stokes), and the signed linear signal A lambda^2 sigma/2. (8) I verified with sympy the 18-node interpolation coefficients (the moment identities sum c_j j^k = delta_{k2} for k <= 17, and the Lagrange x^2 coefficients). I also checked the final scale comparison a_p/h_T + h_T^16 = e^{-15kT/16} + e^{-kT} = o(e^{-14kT/16}). Not independently verified: the Foundation companion inputs (comparison development, first-runout classification, bulk coefficient limits, exterior return rays, beam construction), which are taken as cited.
